result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): Both answers recommend B, work out the roughly 15 hours of team-lead time, and add a short auto-scored gate plus peer role-plays, with no invented statistics. B states the recognize-versus-deliver gap more directly, offers more ways to scale (recordings, re-sessions for reps below the bar, senior-rep facilitators as a fallback) and checks its own numbers. A claims group live rounds cut the lead's time 'further,' but if each rep still gets a 20-minute round, the lead's hours don't drop. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): Both answers recommend B, explain that a multiple-choice test only shows reps can recognize a good answer, work out the roughly 15 hours of lead time, and keep a short auto-scored quiz as a gate. A edges ahead because it gives recorded peer sessions as another option, has a fallback plan if the lead can't spare even 5 hours, and gives the VP a clear pitch. B claims that group live rounds 'cut the lead's time further', which doesn't follow if each rep still gets 20 minutes, though its advice to ask the lead how many hours they have is useful.
